title: Severe hyponatremia & osmotic demyelination syndrome
keyNumbers: 150 mL 3% NaCl IV over 20 min; recheck Na; repeat up to twice more until Na rises 5 mmol/L (ESE 1D/2D)
ESE 2014 correction limits: ≤10 mmol/L in the first 24 h, then ≤8 mmol/L per 24 h until Na 130 (1D)
Verbalis 2013 (US expert panel, ungraded), high ODS risk: limit ≤8 mmol/L in any 24 h; goal 4–6 mmol/L/day. High risk: Na ≤105, hypokalemia, alcohol use disorder, malnutrition, advanced liver disease
Na at 6 h, 12 h, then daily (ESE 2D); if Na ≤120: q4–6h until ≥125 (Verbalis); watch urine output (aquaresis signals overcorrection risk)
presentation: Severe symptoms: vomiting, cardiorespiratory distress, somnolence/coma (GCS ≤8), seizures
ODS (2–6 days after overly rapid correction): dysarthria, dysphagia, quadriparesis, pseudobulbar palsy, locked-in, movement disorders
definitions: ESE 2014 correction limits: ≤10 mmol/L in the first 24 h, then ≤8 mmol/L per 24 h until Na 130 (1D)
Verbalis 2013 (US expert panel, ungraded), high ODS risk: limit ≤8 mmol/L in any 24 h; goal 4–6 mmol/L/day. High risk: Na ≤105, hypokalemia, alcohol use disorder, malnutrition, advanced liver disease

immediateActions.action: 150 mL 3% NaCl IV over 20 min; recheck Na; repeat up to twice more until Na rises 5 mmol/L (ESE 1D/2D)
Stop 3%; keep line open with minimal 0.9% saline; start cause-specific treatment
Na at 6 h, 12 h, then daily (ESE 2D); if Na ≤120: q4–6h until ≥125 (Verbalis); watch urine output (aquaresis signals overcorrection risk)
Re-lower: D5W ± desmopressin if limit exceeded (ESE 1D)

workup.test: Serum osmolality, urine osmolality, urine Na
Volume status and medication review (thiazides, SSRIs, carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine)

notes: Repleting K raises Na — counts toward the correction limit

treatment.doseText: 150 mL over 20 min; repeat up to 2 more times until +5 mmol/L (ESE). SALSA bolus arm: 2 mL/kg (moderate) or 4 mL/kg (severe)
notes: SALSA: rapid intermittent boluses had no more overcorrection than slow infusion (17.2% vs 24.2%) and less need for re-lowering

evidenceNote: ESE 2014: re-lower if >10 in 24 h or >8 in any later 24 h (1D)
Verbalis 2013 (ungraded): high ODS risk, >8 mmol/L in any 24 h may justify re-lowering (S21)

pitfalls: Overcorrection often comes from aquaresis once the cause stops (hypovolemia corrected, thiazide or desmopressin stopped)
escalateWhen: Seizure, coma, or respiratory compromise → ICU
Na rising faster than limits → nephrology, re-lowering
institutionVaries: 3% bolus protocol (150 mL vs 100 mL vs weight-based)
